annotations.title: Scan a live web app for leaked keys and missing protections

description: Reads one public web app the way a browser does (its HTML, the same-site scripts it loads and any source maps they point to) and reports what any visitor can already see: server secret keys shipped to the browser (Supabase service_role, OpenAI, Anthropic, Stripe, AWS, GitHub, SendGrid, Resend; shown masked), a published source map, no HTTPS, and missing Content-Security-Policy, HSTS or frame protection. Use when someone built an app with Lovable, Base44, Bolt, Cursor, Replit or similar and asks whether it is safe to launch or whether a key leaked. It does not sign in, guess paths or query the app's database. Findings are in Hebrew.

url.description: The public address of the app, e.g. my-app.lovable.app or https://example.com
